answer:
The conditions required for password cracking include:

1. **Computational Resources**: A powerful computer with sufficient CPU, RAM, and hard drive space is necessary. The exact requirements depend on the size of the brute force job and the time needed for completion. In some cases, grid or distributed computing may be required for larger tasks.

2. **Skills**: The skill level required is low, as brute force attacks are straightforward. There are many password cracking tools available that facilitate this process [Source 2]. 

These conditions enable an adversary to effectively attempt brute force attacks on passwords.

## Attack description

An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password.

## Required resources

A powerful enough computer for the job with sufficient CPU, RAM and HD. Exact requirements will depend on the size of the brute force job and the time requirement for completion. Some brute forcing jobs may require grid or distributed computing (e.g. DES Challenge).

## Required skills

Low: A brute force attack is very straightforward. A variety of password cracking tools are widely available.

## Consequences

Brute forcing credentials may take place at various points during a breach. For example, adversaries may attempt to brute force access to [Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078) within a victim environment leveraging knowledge gathered from other post-compromise behaviors such as [OS Credential Dumping](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003), [Account Discovery](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087), or [Password Policy
